It would be a lie to tell y'all I been eating pretty 100%. There have been more tribulations than trials though! There was even one dish that tasted better when I re-fried the leftovers. So this is an easy art to pick up.

Finally got an induction grill and have been cooking my own meals 4 times a week for the first time in 30 years. I got into the habit of eating out and never had anything at home except emergency crap.

Induction grills work by using magnetic fields to disturb any magnetically reactive particles in the cookware itself. This means it heats up the pan, not the stove. The difference is incredible. What I usually do is put something in on low. At this point it doesn't matter if one item is frozen or not, though I tend to make sure something is semi-defrosted and not bricklike before using it. [Omaha steaks come to mind. Usually a couple days before they are ready to throw in from the delivery container]

I can leave something in on low for 20-45 minutes while doing other things, and just check on it once or twice with the spatula to flip. Another thing I have figured out is the frying pan I ended up with is 1" diameter larger than my 10" induction cooktop, so I can easily create cooler areas. [If a dish has a lot of gravy or sauce and it is getting cooked off it can be moved to the edge and the pan can be moved to eliminate any direct heating of that portion of the pan due to the induction method]

Anyway the first Stainless Steel pan for the cooktop I bought was too pure to work. Cast Iron works great but I found a Combo Ceramic/Steel pan that works beautifully. Saved the original Stainless pan for propane/charcoal grilling.

Honey Beet Chicken

1/2 lb Chicken Breast, pre-seasoned with lemon-pepper and italian garden seasonings.

1 Cup diced beets

2 tsp beet juice

2 tsp honey

Bring the pan to 1/4 temp. Drop the beet cubes and the beet juice into a concentrated area.

Set the pre-seasoned breast down on top of the beet cubes.

Dump all the honey on top of the chicken breast

Wait until the outermost edges of the beet juice have started to boil off, then flip the breast over without spilling any honey

wait until all the beet juice outside the beet cube substrate has boiled off, then put the chicken directly on the pan and move all the beet cubes on top of the chicken

get all the sauce too, up on top of the chicken

let it cook until the bottom of the chicken seems dry
